newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended mostly firmer on Wednesday, though the short end lost a little ground, after shooting higher with other markets in early trade. Fading bunds shaved back the gains into the close, dealers said.

The Finance Ministry closed its new tap issue of 5.75 percent 2007 bonds, saying a total of 7.5 billion guilders had been raised. This falls short of the 10 billion or so required for a liquid new market benchmark, one trader said.
The last day of the tap sparked lively trade at the long end, he added, with demand for the new issue picking up after sluggish retail on Tuesday.
Around 2.8 billion guilders worth of the Feb 2007s were shifted on Wednesday, compared to 1.1 billion on Tuesday.

The issue traded at an average price of 100.85 and yield of 5.64 percent, the ministry said. Compared with fair-value 10-year yields of around 5.70, this made the bond quite expensive, one analyst said.
Traders see the ministry possibly reopening the issue later in the year to get it up to 10 billion in size. Many do not expect more borrowing than that to be necessary this year.
Guilders outperformed bunds with the 10-year spread to the April 2006 bund moving to test minus 15 basis points.

The guilder market should retain a relatively positive tone in the next few days, traders said, with prices, particularly at the long end, well supported. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
